findings.reason: the builder must be told whether the admission pass skips a request overlapping a live worker claim (no failure recorded) or lets the scope check refuse it and stamp a failure each pass, because the second is exactly the per-pass failure recording §18 exists to stop, and the plan's own §4 evidence (`c-s4-withdraw-loop`, `c-s4-head-of-queue-starved`) treats that repeated failure as the flicker the queue is meant to remove.
findings.text: §18's deliverable states that once the earlier request launches "its worker's real claim keeps the later one waiting in the same way, until that run is promoted or discarded", where "in the same way" is the immediately preceding treatment of "leaves that request queued behind the earlier one and records no failure"; but the same deliverable requires "every phase other than `queued` binds as today", and after launch the earlier request's pointer is in a non-`queued` phase (`starting`/`launching`/`working`, no pid yet), which `claim_disposition` binds (`reckon/crew/node.py:1485`) so the scope check refuses the later request's relaunch (`reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:1588`, `:1673`) and the admission pass records a failure on it every pass (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:618`–`:642`)

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_repository_scope_claims`, `claim_disposition`, `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py`, and `tests/test_a_node_is_queued_once.py::test_a_different_node_over_a_claimed_path_is_still_refused` all resolve, and the two cited 2026-10-13 cases match their supporting comment (`c-s18-lost-request-during-deadlock`).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — the five cases are measurable, and the section declares a negative control ("count queued pointers as claims again") that reddens the queued-over-queued cases.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the control is "logged under the run directory", a durable crew-home path, not a session scratchpad or node-local temp.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers reach code; the phase vocabulary (`queued`, `starting`, `working`) and the test names describe mechanism.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the deliverable says a launched earlier request keeps the later one "waiting in the same way" (i.e. queued behind, no failure), yet also says "every phase other than `queued` binds as today", and the launched run is no longer in the `queued` phase.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable: how the scope check and the admission pass treat a queued pointer's claim.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §18 declares it runs after §14, whose case it partly supersedes, and before §15, which also writes `queue_admission.py`; it names the §12 cap it must still honour, and every file and test it cites resolves.
